ai.title: Conditional tool and agent prompt generation
ai.summary: Agent prompt generation now conditionally appends tool instructions and spawnable agent descriptions only when present. Previously, empty sections were always added to the instructionsPrompt. This change affects `packages/agent-runtime/src/templates/strings.ts`. The fix prevents unnecessary whitespace and empty text blocks in the final prompt string.

eli5.text: When the assistant builds its instructions during a run, it now only adds the section about available tools and the section about spawnable agents when those actually exist. If an agent has no tools or no spawnable agents, those empty blocks are skipped instead of being appended as blank space. You would notice cleaner, more predictable instruction text with no stray empty paragraphs. The change lives on today in the agent-runtime package.

ai.title: Base2 validation standardization
ai.summary: The `base2-fast-with-validation` agent definition is removed from `.agents/base2/`. The `createBase2` factory in `.agents/base2/base2.ts` now accepts only `fast` or `max` modes. Validation steps (typechecks, tests, lints) are integrated directly into the prompt logic for both `fast` and `max` modes, ensuring standard behavior without a separate variant.

eli5.text: The assistant used to have two ways to run: a quick mode that skipped checking your work, and a quick mode that also checked it. Now there's just one quick mode, and it always checks your work the same way (running type checks, tests, lints) before finishing. If you used the separate checking variant, it's gone; the quick mode now includes checking by default. Developers who relied on that separate option will need to switch to the standard quick mode, which behaves the same as the old checking variant did. This is live today: both quick and full-power modes now run validation steps as part of their process, with no separate variant to choose.

ai.title: New task-researcher2, planner-pro, gpt-5-worker agent iteration
ai.summary: Added task-researcher2 (claude-sonnet-4.5, structured output with report+relevantFiles) and planner-pro-with-files-input (gpt-5-pro, no tools, deep-thinking implementation plans). base2-with-task-researcher now spawns task-researcher2 and planner-pro-with-files-input instead of task-researcher/code-reviewer/validator, gains spawn_agent_inline tool, and swaps generate-plan for planner-pro. base2-gpt-5-worker simplified: stepPrompt removed, final step changed from "inform parent to double-check" to "end your turn". Files: .agents/researcher/task-researcher2.ts, .agents/planners/planner-pro-with-files-input.ts, .agents/base2/base2-gpt-5-worker.ts, .agents/base2/task-researcher/base2-with-task-researcher.ts.

eli5.text: When you ask the assistant to tackle a coding task, it now follows a two-step research plan. First, a smarter research agent explores your codebase, gathers the key facts, and produces a written report plus a list of the files that matter for your request. Then a deep-thinking planning agent takes that report and file list to draft a detailed implementation plan, which a separate coding agent will later carry out. The practical effect is that before any code gets written for your request, the assistant pauses to read the relevant parts of the project it hadn't seen yet, rather than guessing from memory. You won't notice the extra step, but the resulting suggestions should fit your existing project structure more closely.

ai.title: Step prompt wrapping now requires non-empty prompt
ai.summary: Step prompt wrapping now requires a non-empty prompt value before applying <system_reminder> tags. This prevents empty step prompts from being wrapped and sent to the agent. Scope limited to packages/agent-runtime/src/templates/strings.ts. The condition adds a truthy check for prompt alongside existing type and agentType checks.

eli5.text: When you (as an assistant) try to save a quick note or reminder to yourself about what to do next, the system used to let that note be completely blank and still slap a special tag on it. Now, the system only adds that special tag when the note actually has some text in it. An empty note gets ignored, so you won't see useless blank reminders being passed around in the background. This change is already live and affects how step-by-step instructions are handled behind the scenes.

eli5.text: The chat-completion endpoint became more forgiving when the incoming request body is missing the stream setting or the optional metadata attached to codebuff runs. You would only notice if your automated tool calls sometimes omit those fields and previously broke the flow; now they no longer crash. Nothing else visible changes today for regular chat use. This is already live and mainly stabilizes the path for internal tooling that builds completion requests.

ai.title: Refactor SDK stream chunk handling and tool XML filtering
ai.summary: The `handleStreamChunk` callback in `sdk/src/run.ts` now accepts a union of strings and structured `subagent_chunk` objects, moving subagent delta accumulation logic from `cli/src/hooks/use-send-message.ts` into the SDK boundary. `sdk/src/tool-xml-filter.ts` is rewritten to use an async `filterXml` function with `startToolTag`/`endToolTag` constants, replacing the previous stateful `ToolXmlFilterState` and buffer management. `sdk/src/tool-xml-buffer.ts` is deleted, and its exports are removed from `sdk/src/index.ts`. The CLI hook simplifies by delegating raw string vs object handling directly to the new SDK event shape.

eli5.text: When you chat with multiple AI assistants at once, their responses now stream more smoothly and reliably to your screen. The system was reorganized so that the way text pieces (chunks) are stitched together and filtered behind the scenes moved from the chat interface into the core engine that powers all AI conversations. This means the same reliable streaming logic is now shared everywhere the software is used, instead of being duplicated in just the chat window. You won't see a new button or setting, but you should notice fewer glitches and interruptions when assistants are typing their replies in real time.

ai.title: filterXml switches from callback to generator stream
ai.summary: sdk/src/tool-xml-filter.ts changes filterXml from an async function with an omit callback to a synchronous generator yielding {chunk} objects. sdk/src/run.ts updates onStreamChunk and onSubagentResponseChunk to consume the stream via while(true) loop and await handleStreamChunk per yielded chunk. Internal refactor for streaming tool XML filtering.

eli5.text: When an assistant streams a response that includes tool calls (the special XML blocks the AI uses to invoke functions), the SDK now processes those blocks chunk-by-chunk in real time instead of feeding them through a callback that runs after the whole response arrives. This means you see the assistant's regular text flow more smoothly, with tool-call tags filtered out as the stream comes in, rather than having them cleaned up in a separate pass. The change live as of October 25, 2025, affects anyone building on the SDK to handle streamed agent responses, and the behavior is noticeable if you're consuming those chunks directly in your application.

The assistant's user profile lookup was also split into a smaller, self-checking piece so the system can catch errors sooner and keep the default profile fields (like ID) intact, leaving your experience unchanged.

eli5.text: The software toolkit for building AI-powered coding assistants has been given a new release number, moving from its previous version to the next one. This new release matches the point where the toolkit now includes a local runtime, meaning the AI agent can run directly on a user's machine without needing to connect to external services. The change is purely a version update in the toolkit's configuration file, affecting developers who integrate this toolkit into their projects. If you looked at the toolkit's files today, you would see the updated version number reflecting this new milestone.

eli5.text: Starting today, the base2 agent uses a single file-researcher tool to locate relevant files in one pass, instead of spawning multiple file-picker tools in separate steps. When you look, you'll see the agent first consults file-researcher to find all relevant files, then reads them all at once in a single pass, before optionally gathering more context as needed. The older multi-step approach of spawning file-pickers and reading files repeatedly has been replaced with this streamlined workflow.

eli5.text: The code-writing assistant now refuses to take shortcuts that make its work harder to check. ai.title: Add Windows troubleshooting guide to WINDOWS.md
ai.summary: WINDOWS.md gains Common Windows Issues & Troubleshooting section. Covers failed version checks, git command syntax errors, login browser launch failures, and update message confusion. Provides specific fixes for corporate proxies, Git Bash/WSL compatibility, and manual login URL handling. References issues #294, #274, and #299.

eli5.text: If you use Codebuff on Windows and run into problems, you now have a single place to look for fixes instead of hunting through scattered help pages. The documentation added a troubleshooting section covering four common stumbling blocks: the program can’t reach GitHub to check for updates on certain networks, git commands fail with syntax errors in the Windows command prompt, the login browser window doesn’ pop open automatically, and update notifications look like errors but are just informational. Each entry explains what the message means and walks you through the steps that resolve it, including how to work around corporate firewalls and how to manually open the login link when the automatic browser launch fails. This went live today, open WINDOWS.md and scroll down to the Common

ai.title: formatCodeSearchOutput returns No results on empty stdout
ai.summary: Added guard in `formatCodeSearchOutput` to return 'No results' when `stdout` is empty. Prevents downstream processing of empty strings and ensures consistent user-facing output. Change scoped to `common/src/util/format-code-search.ts`.

eli5.text: When you search for code and nothing matches, you now see the words "No results" instead of a blank space where a message should be. Previously, the system would try to display a list even when there wasn't one, which sometimes caused confusion or unexpected follow-up steps. Now, an empty search result is immediately replaced with a clear notice, so you know the search just didn't find anything rather than wondering if something broke.
